title: The Highland Owl
teaser: A necklace vanished from a sleeper train somewhere between Preston and Carlisle. The train was searched from end to end. It wasn't on board.

booklet.briefing:
The Highland Owl leaves London at 9:15 pm and arrives in Inverness at 8:40 the next morning. Mrs. Ottoline Sand, travelling in sleeper compartment C14, went to bed at 00:50 with her emerald necklace on the shelf beside her pillow.

At 02:00 the train braked hard on the way into Carlisle and she woke. The necklace was gone. The latch on her door had been reported broken before the journey.

At Perth, at 05:50, police searched the whole train: every passenger, every bag, every compartment. No necklace. Mr. Foxy thinks the necklace left the train, and that tells you more than it seems.
rules: The necklace was taken between 00:50 and 02:00.
The train's windows are sealed and cannot be opened. The only stops between 00:50 and the Perth search were Carlisle (02:10) and nowhere else.

setting.place: The Highland Owl sleeper train, London to Inverness

suspects.name: Leon Ferris
suspects.description: Next door to Mrs. Sand. A professional card player.
suspects.motive: Lost heavily at cards earlier in the evening.
suspects.statement: I went to the lounge car for a game at twenty to one and didn't come back till gone two. Ask the barman.

suspects.name: Professor Hilda Ames
suspects.description: An elderly geologist who sleeps with a breathing machine for her sleep apnoea.
suspects.motive: Her research grant has been cut and she needs money.
suspects.statement: I was asleep with my mask on from half past twelve. I didn't hear a thing.

suspects.name: Mr. Kenneth Dunlop
suspects.description: A retired jeweller. Recognised Mrs. Sand's emeralds at dinner and told her what they were worth.
suspects.motive: Knows exactly what the necklace is worth and how to sell it.
suspects.statement: My door was jammed. I couldn't have got out if I'd wanted to.

suspects.name: Miss Annabel Cho
suspects.description: Quiet, polite, travelling light. Booked only as far as Carlisle.
suspects.statement: I slept until the attendant knocked to say we were nearly at Carlisle, then I got off. I'm visiting my aunt.

suspects.name: Mr. Toby Rook
suspects.description: Couldn't afford a sleeper and sat up all night. Got off at Carlisle.
suspects.motive: Was seen admiring the necklace in the dining car.
suspects.statement: I was in my seat in Coach A all night, except getting a glass of water for that poor lady who was ill. Then I got off at Carlisle.

evidence.title: How the train is laid out
evidence.body:
From front to back: Coach A (seats) – Lounge car – Coach B (sleepers B1–B10) – Coach C (sleepers C11–C20).

Coach C is at the very back. There is no door beyond it. The only way into or out of Coach C, while the train is moving, is through the vestibule between Coach B and Coach C.

Coach C has its own outside door, opened only at stations.

evidence.title: Attendant's vestibule log
evidence.source: Hamish Grant, attendant, desk in the B–C vestibule
evidence.body:
Hamish logs everyone who passes between Coach B and Coach C overnight. Nobody else passed between 00:30 and 03:00.

Time | Entry
00:40 | Mr. Ferris (C13), C to B, going to the lounge.
01:20 | Called to Coach A: passenger taken ill. Desk unattended.
01:36 | Back at desk.
01:58 | Knocked on C18 (Miss Cho) to wake her for Carlisle, as she asked. She answered at once, dressed.
02:01 | Mrs. Sand (C14) rings the call bell: necklace missing.
02:15 | Mr. Ferris, B to C, back from the lounge.

evidence.title: Hamish, about Coach A
evidence.body: “From 01:20 to 01:36 I was with the lady who was ill in Coach A. Mr. Rook sat across the aisle the whole time and fetched her water from the tap at the end of Coach A. He never left the coach while I was there.”

evidence.title: The lounge barman
evidence.body: “Mr. Ferris played cards at the corner table from quarter to one until ten past two. He never left the table; he was winning back his money and wouldn't leave it for a second.”

evidence.title: Professor Ames's breathing machine
evidence.body: Mask on: 00:31. Mask off: 05:41. No breaks. The machine stops and logs an alarm if the mask comes off for more than 10 seconds.

evidence.title: Fault report, C16
evidence.body:
21:30: C16 door handle broken; door can only be opened from the corridor with the attendant's tool. Passenger informed. To be repaired at Inverness.

Hamish: “I didn't open C16 for anyone until the police did at Perth.”

evidence.title: Carlisle platform camera
evidence.body:
Only two passengers got off at Carlisle: Miss Cho, from Coach C's door, with a small wheeled case; and Mr. Rook, from Coach A's door, with a rucksack.

Nobody got on.

evidence.title: Carlisle police, Wednesday 9:00 am
evidence.body: Miss Cho was traced to a hotel near the station, not her aunt's. In the lining of her washbag: an emerald necklace, identified by Mrs. Sand.

questions.explanation: The necklace left at Carlisle, so the thief is Miss Cho or Mr. Rook. Rook was in Coach A with the attendant during the only unguarded window, and couldn't reach Coach C at any other time without being logged. Miss Cho was already in Coach C, answered her door dressed at 01:58, and the necklace was in her washbag.
hints: Two people got off at Carlisle. Can you clear one?
The other was already inside Coach C and didn't need the gap at all.
Who answered her door fully dressed at 01:58, 'having slept until then'?

solution.explanation: Annabel Cho booked compartment C18 only as far as Carlisle, the first stop after the small hours. Already in Coach C, she never needed to pass the attendant's desk. Shortly before 02:00 she slipped into C14 through the broken-latched door, took the emeralds from the shelf, and was back and dressed when Hamish knocked at 01:58. Ten minutes later she stepped off at Carlisle with the necklace in her washbag, long before the police searched the train at Perth.

chain.step: The necklace wasn't on board at Perth, the windows are sealed, and Carlisle was the only stop. It left at Carlisle.
Only Miss Cho and Mr. Rook got off at Carlisle.
To reach Coach C, Rook would have had to pass the desk. The desk was only empty from 01:20 to 01:36, while Hamish was with Rook in Coach A.
Miss Cho was in Coach C all along, and answered her door already dressed at 01:58.
The necklace was found in her washbag.

eliminations.name: Leon Ferris
eliminations.why: At the lounge card table from 00:45 to 02:10 per the barman, logged back into Coach C at 02:15, and didn't get off at Carlisle.

eliminations.name: Professor Hilda Ames
eliminations.why: Her breathing machine shows the mask on without a break from 00:31 to 05:41, and she stayed on the train.

eliminations.name: Mr. Kenneth Dunlop
eliminations.why: His door could only be opened from the corridor with the attendant's tool, and nobody opened it until Perth.

eliminations.name: Mr. Toby Rook
eliminations.why: In Coach A, watched by the attendant, during the only time the B–C vestibule was unguarded.
